newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat assails Jewish housing for East Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Arafat assails Jewish housing for East Jerusalem.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Wednesday an Israeli plan to build 132 housing units for Jews in the heart of Arab East Jerusalem violated interim peace deals with the PLO.
"This is a very serious breaching for what has been agreed upon," Arafat, speaking in English, told reporters.

The future of East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed, is to be determined only in final-status peace talks which have yet to resume under Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who took office in June.
Israel's Jerusalem municipal planning commission approved on Tuesday a plan for Jewish housing in the Ras al-Amoud neighbourhood, where about 11,000 Palestinians live.
It needs ministerial approval, which could take months, to go ahead.
Faisal al-Husseini, the leading PLO representative in Jerusalem, has called the decision a "time bomb" and said it would ignite a new outburst of violence if implemented.

He was referring to a wave of violence in September sparked by Israel's opening an entrance to an archaeological tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem. Sixty Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in the clashes.
Israel has encircled Arab East Jerusalem with Jewish neighbourhoods since it captured the city along with the rest of the West Bank in 1967.
But apart from the settling of some 3,000 Jews inside the walled Old City, it would be the first time that Israel had tried to settle Jews in the heart of an Arab community.

Some 160,000 Jews and about 155,000 Palestinians live in East Jerusalem. The PLO wants East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state. Israel regards the city as part of its "eternal" capital.
